use: More emotional and bookish than ryokou; used for long or solo trips, and in songs and titles.

example.romaji: itsuka hitori de tabi shite mitai na.
example.ja: いつか一人で旅してみたいな。
example.english: I'd love to travel on my own someday.

examplePolite.romaji: itsuka hitori de tabi o shite mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: いつか一人で旅をしてみたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like to travel on my own someday.

notes: For a normal holiday trip, ryokou is the safe word.

use: Picking up kids from daycare or someone from the station; omukae ni iku = go and pick up.

example.romaji: gogo, kodomo no omukae ni ikanakya.
example.ja: 午後、子どものお迎えに行かなきゃ。
example.english: I have to go pick up my kid this afternoon.

examplePolite.romaji: gogo wa kodomo no omukae ni ikanai to ikenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 午後は子どものお迎えに行かないといけないんです。
examplePolite.english: I have to go pick up my child this afternoon.

notes: Plain mukae means the same: eki made mukae ni iku yo (I'll come get you at the station). The verb is mukaeru.

example.romaji: gakkou made jitensha de juppun gurai.
example.ja: 学校まで自転車で10分ぐらい。
example.english: It's about ten minutes to school by bike.

examplePolite.romaji: gakkou made jitensha de juppun gurai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 学校まで自転車で10分ぐらいです。
examplePolite.english: It's about ten minutes to school by bike.

notes: Casually called chari; a city bike with a basket is a mamachari.

use: Both the spring and the bath or town built around it.

example.romaji: shuumatsu, onsen demo ikitai na.
example.ja: 週末、温泉でも行きたいな。
example.english: I'd love to go to a hot spring this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu wa onsen ni demo ikitai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 週末は温泉にでも行きたいですね。
examplePolite.english: I'd love to go to a hot spring this weekend.

notes: Onsen ni hairu = take a dip. A town bathhouse without spring water is a sentou.

use: A soft word for an outing, often with kids or a partner; odekake suru = go out.

example.romaji: kyou wa tenki ii kara, odekake shiyou ka.
example.ja: 今日は天気いいから、お出かけしようか。
example.english: The weather's nice today, shall we go out somewhere?

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa tenki ga ii node, odekake shimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は天気がいいので、お出かけしましょうか。
examplePolite.english: The weather's nice today, so shall we go out somewhere?

notes: Neighbours greet you with odekake desu ka? (heading out?). The verb is dekakeru.

use: A group drinking session with coworkers, classmates or friends, usually at an izakaya.

example.romaji: kyou nomikai da kara, bangohan iranai.
example.ja: 今日飲み会だから、晩ご飯いらない。
example.english: I've got a work drinks thing tonight, so I don't need dinner.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa nomikai ga aru node, bangohan wa irimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は飲み会があるので、晩ご飯はいりません。
examplePolite.english: I have a drinking party tonight, so I won't need dinner.

notes: The second round somewhere else is the nijikai.

use: Directions are given by them: tsugi no shingou (the next light).

example.romaji: tsugi no shingou o migi ni magatte.
example.ja: 次の信号を右に曲がって。
example.english: Turn right at the next light.

examplePolite.romaji: tsugi no shingou o migi ni magatte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 次の信号を右に曲がってください。
examplePolite.english: Please turn right at the next light.

notes: The green light is called ao (blue): shingou ga ao ni natta.

example.romaji: yabai, shuuden nogashichatta kamo.
example.ja: やばい、終電逃しちゃったかも。
example.english: Oh no, I think I missed the last train.

examplePolite.romaji: shuuden o nogashite shimatta kamo shiremasen.
examplePolite.ja: 終電を逃してしまったかもしれません。
examplePolite.english: I may have missed the last train.

notes: Goes with nogasu (miss) and ni maniau (make it in time).

example.romaji: juutai de zenzen ugokanai.
example.ja: 渋滞で全然動かない。
example.english: We're stuck in traffic, not moving at all.

examplePolite.romaji: juutai de zenzen ugokimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 渋滞で全然動きません。
examplePolite.english: We're stuck in traffic and not moving at all.

notes: Also juutai suru (be jammed): michi ga juutai shiteru.

use: The rush-hour train where you can't move; man'in alone means full to capacity.

example.romaji: maiasa man'in densha de tsukareru yo.
example.ja: 毎朝満員電車で疲れるよ。
example.english: The packed train every morning wears me out.

examplePolite.romaji: maiasa man'in densha de tsukaremasu.
examplePolite.ja: 毎朝満員電車で疲れます。
examplePolite.english: The packed train every morning wears me out.

use: Both grocery runs and fun shopping; kaimono ni iku = go shopping.

example.romaji: chotto kaimono itte kuru ne.
example.ja: ちょっと買い物行ってくるね。
example.english: I'm just popping out to do some shopping.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto kaimono ni itte kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと買い物に行ってきます。
examplePolite.english: I'm just going out to do some shopping.

use: Money owed, to a bank or a person.

example.romaji: kare, kekkou shakkin aru rashii yo.
example.ja: 彼、結構借金あるらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently he's got quite a lot of debt.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kekkou shakkin ga aru rashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は結構借金があるらしいです。
examplePolite.english: Apparently he has quite a lot of debt.

notes: Shakkin suru = borrow money; shakkin o kaesu = pay it back. A small loan from a friend is just kariru.

use: Phone plans, apartments, jobs; anything you sign up to.

example.romaji: kinou, atarashii heya no keiyaku shite kita.
example.ja: 昨日、新しい部屋の契約してきた。
example.english: I signed the contract for my new place yesterday.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou, atarashii heya no keiyaku o shite kimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日、新しい部屋の契約をしてきました。
examplePolite.english: I signed the contract for my new apartment yesterday.

notes: Keiyaku suru = sign a contract; keiyaku ga kireru = it runs out.

english: service; something free, on the house
use: In shops and restaurants it often means a freebie.

example.romaji: kono koohii, saabisu datte.
example.ja: このコーヒー、サービスだって。
example.english: They said this coffee's on the house.

examplePolite.romaji: kono koohii wa saabisu da sou desu.
examplePolite.ja: このコーヒーはサービスだそうです。
examplePolite.english: I'm told this coffee is on the house.

notes: Staff say kore, saabisu desu (this one's on us). Saabisu zangyou is unpaid overtime.

use: At a restaurant or online; the noun chuumon is the order itself.

example.romaji: mou nanika chuumon shita?
example.ja: もう何か注文した？
example.english: Have you ordered anything yet?

examplePolite.romaji: mou nanika chuumon shimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: もう何か注文しましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you ordered anything yet?

notes: Staff ask gochuumon wa okimari desu ka? (ready to order?). When ordering, people mostly just say X onegai shimasu.

use: At a till it usually means a credit card; kaado de = by card.

example.romaji: koko tte kaado tsukaeru kana?
example.ja: ここってカード使えるかな？
example.english: Do you think they take cards here?

examplePolite.romaji: kaado wa tsukaemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: カードは使えますか？
examplePolite.english: Do you take cards?

notes: The full word is kurejitto kaado.

use: Store points come up at almost every till: pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka?

example.romaji: pointo tamatta kara, tada de kaeta.
example.ja: ポイント貯まったから、タダで買えた。
example.english: I'd saved up points, so I got it for free.

examplePolite.romaji: pointo ga tamatta node, tada de kaemashita.
examplePolite.ja: ポイントが貯まったので、タダで買えました。
examplePolite.english: I'd saved up points, so I got it for free.

notes: Also the key part: koko ga pointo (this is what matters).

use: Shop and business talk; for stuff you bought, people just say mono.

example.romaji: kono shouhin, mou urikire datte.
example.ja: この商品、もう売り切れだって。
example.english: They said this item's already sold out.

examplePolite.romaji: kono shouhin wa mou urikire desu.
examplePolite.ja: この商品はもう売り切れです。
examplePolite.english: This item is already sold out.

notes: Shinshouhin (new product) is all over menus and packaging.

example.romaji: kore, nedan no wari ni oishii ne.
example.ja: これ、値段の割においしいね。
example.english: This is really good for the price.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa nedan no wari ni oishii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: これは値段の割においしいですね。
examplePolite.english: This is really good for the price.

notes: To ask a price you just say ikura? Nedan ga takai / yasui = pricey / cheap.

example.romaji: kanojo no ie, sugoi kanemochi rashii yo.
example.ja: 彼女の家、すごい金持ちらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently her family's really rich.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo no ie wa sugoku okanemochi rashii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女の家はすごくお金持ちらしいです。
examplePolite.english: Apparently her family is very wealthy.

notes: Okanemochi is the softer, more common form. The opposite is binbou (poor).
